plan.contextChunk: This figure contains two 2D vectors emanating from a common origin, illustrating the geometric definition of endpoint error in optical flow evaluation. The vector labeled (u, v) represents the ground truth flow vector, while the vector labeled (u-hat, v-hat) represents the predicted flow vector; both share the same base point but point in slightly different directions and have different magnitudes. A red line segment connects the tips (endpoints) of the two vectors, and this segment is labeled Endpoint error, making explicit that the loss is the Euclidean distance between the endpoint of the prediction and the endpoint of the ground truth. This figure establishes endpoint error as a vector-space distance metric, clarifying why it is sensitive to both directional and magnitude errors in the predicted flow field.

interactionPlan.concept: Endpoint error measures the Euclidean distance between the tip of a predicted optical flow vector and the tip of the ground-truth vector, so a single number captures both directional and magnitude mistakes.
elements: common origin point at lower left where both vectors begin
ground-truth flow vector: black arrow pointing steeply up-right, labeled (u,v) in italic serif near its tip
predicted flow vector: black arrow pointing shallower up-right, shorter and less steep than ground truth, labeled (û,v̂) with hat accents near its tip
red straight segment connecting the two vector tips, labeled 'Endpoint error' to its right
angular-error arc between the two vectors near the origin, labeled 'Angular error' (visible only in angular-error mode)
numeric readout of the current error value (distance in pixels or angle in degrees)

interactions.teaches: The endpoint error is exactly the distance from the prediction's tip to the ground truth's tip — moving (û,v̂) in any direction stretches or shrinks the red segment, and it vanishes only when the two tips coincide

The error is relative to the reference flow: changing the ground-truth vector's direction or length repositions the red segment even if the prediction stays fixed, so the same prediction can be good for one true motion and poor for another

interactions.label: Error metric
interactions.teaches: Endpoint error measures the straight-line distance between vector tips and is therefore sensitive to both direction and magnitude, while angular error measures only the angle between the vectors and ignores how long they are

demo_steps.title: Two vectors, one origin
demo_steps.narration: The ground-truth flow (u,v) and the prediction (û,v̂) start at the same pixel. The red segment joining their tips is the endpoint error — the Euclidean distance between where the flow should point and where the estimate says it points.

demo_steps.title: Move the prediction
demo_steps.narration: Drag the tip of (û,v̂): the red segment stretches as the estimate drifts from the truth and shrinks to zero only when the tips coincide — matching either direction or magnitude alone is not enough.

demo_steps.title: Move the ground truth
demo_steps.narration: Now drag (u,v): with the prediction held fixed, the error still changes, showing endpoint error is a property of the pair of vectors, not of the prediction alone.

demo_steps.title: Compare with angular error
demo_steps.narration: Switch to angular error: only the wedge between the vectors is highlighted. A short vector and a long vector in the same direction have zero angular error but nonzero endpoint error — the two metrics penalize different mistakes.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: Endpoint error is the tip-to-tip distance between prediction and ground truth, so one scalar simultaneously penalizes wrong direction and wrong magnitude — unlike angular error, which only sees direction.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: White background, no axes — just the shared origin at lower left. Both arrows are thick black with filled triangular arrowheads; the ground-truth arrow (u,v) is steeper and slightly longer, the predicted arrow (û,v̂) shallower and shorter, so their tips are clearly separated. Labels in large italic serif math type: (u,v) above-left of the upper tip, (û,v̂) below-right of the lower tip with visible hat diacritics. The red connector is a thick straight segment between the tips with 'Endpoint error' in plain serif text to its right. Both tips are draggable handles; the red segment and numeric readout update live. In angular-error mode, fade the red segment and instead draw a small arc near the origin between the two vector directions with the angle value, keeping the vectors themselves unchanged.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Drag the estimated vector tip (û,v̂) in any direction and see the red endpoint error segment stretch or shrink in real time as the distance between the two vector tips updates
- Drag the ground-truth vector tip (u,v) to set a new reference flow direction and magnitude, watching the red error segment reposition accordingly
- Toggle between endpoint error (straight-line distance between vector tips) and angular error (angle between the two vectors) metrics, highlighting which geometric quantity each measures in the diagram

- Drag the estimated vector tip (û,v̂) in any direction and see the red endpoint error segment stretch or shrink in real time as the distance between the two vector tips updates
- Drag the ground-truth vector tip (u,v) to set a new reference flow direction and magnitude, watching the red error segment reposition accordingly

authoredContext: In supervised optical flow estimation, the most common loss is the **endpoint error**, which is the average, over the whole image, if the distance between the estimated optical flow vector, $(\hat{u},\hat{v})$ and the ground-truth vector, $(u,v)$: $$\mathcal{L} \left( \hat{\mathbf{u}}, \hat{\mathbf{v}}, \mathbf{u}, \mathbf{v} \right) = \sum_{n,m} (\hat{u}[n,m] - u[n,m])^2 + (\hat{v}[n,m] - v[n,m])^2$$ The sum is over all the pixels in the image. Each pixel has an estimated optical flow $(\hat{u}[n,m],\hat{v}[n,m])$.

discrepancies: both arrow tips are capped by black circular drag handles and the origin is marked with a black dot, whereas the source arrows end in clean bare arrowheads emanating from an unadorned point
the circumflex on v in '(û,v̂)' renders as a detached floating caret to the right of the v instead of sitting directly over the letter as in the source
a bold readout ('Endpoint error = 202 px' / 'Angular error = 21.7°') occupies the top-left of the figure area, prominent text that does not exist in the source
in the source the red 'Endpoint error' segment visibly joins the two arrowheads; here the junctions are visually covered by the handle dots
evaluation.notes: The core figure — two shared-origin black arrows, steep/long (u,v) vs shallow/short (û,v̂), red tip-to-tip endpoint-error segment, and correct serif labels — is faithfully reproduced, and the draggable tips, endpoint/angular metric toggle, and 4-step demo player are all functional and pedagogically strong; the main blemishes are the handle dots covering the arrowheads and the detached hat glyph on v.
action_items: Render the v-hat cleanly (e.g. as a separately positioned '̂' glyph or by composing the label from two text elements) so '(û,v̂)' matches the source instead of showing a floating caret.

Make the tip drag handles and origin dot visually subordinate (smaller, outline-only, or revealed on hover) so the arrows appear to end in clean arrowheads and the red segment visibly meets the tips as in the source.
Consider toning down or relocating the bold top-left readout so the default state reads more like the unadorned source figure.
